### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19 and A25 were not observed in any of the 200 traces and A20 in only 1; in the later window A19 runs in about 38% of traces (76 of 200), A25 in about 35% (69) and A20 in about 30% (59), each at most once per trace and around 0.35–0.37 of the trace length. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- In the earlier window, A26 immediately followed A41 in about 82% of traces; in the later window that direct adjacency almost disappears (about 1%) and A26 instead follows A41 two steps later in about 83% of cases. [LAG001]
- A41's outgoing transitions changed accordingly: A26 took about 82% of A41's observed outgoing transitions earlier and about 1.5% later, while about 33% now go to A19, 30% to A25 and 24% to A20. [DIR004]
- The new activities lead on to A26: about 95% of A19's and about 90% of A25's observed outgoing transitions go to A26; A19 precedes A26 in about 37.5% of later traces and A25 in about 32.5%, while A41 precedes A19, A25 and A20 in about 37.5%, 33% and 28% of traces. [DIR002, DIR003, REL003, REL008, REL004, REL009, REL007, REL006]
- A19, A20 and A25 behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: any two of them co-occur in only about 0.5–1.5% of later traces, so nearly every later trace contains at most one of the three. [REL001, REL002, REL005]
- A26 and A41 still occur in essentially all traces in both windows; A26's mean position moves slightly later, from about 0.37 to about 0.40 of the trace length. [POS004, REL004]
- Separately, A02's outgoing profile redistributed: A26 received about 26% of A02's observed outgoing transitions earlier and none later, A16 rose from about 9% to about 18%, and many small new successors appeared (A02 seen in 35 vs 44 traces). [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, a one-of-three choice among A19, A20 and A25 runs between A41 and A26, where earlier A26 followed A41 directly. The successor change is observed directly at the source: A26 falls from about 82% to about 1.5% of A41's observed outgoing transitions while A19, A25 and A20 take about 87% together, and A19 and A25 in turn lead to A26 in about 95% and 90% of their outgoing transitions. The relational and distance evidence agrees — A41 precedes each of the three and each of the three precedes A26 in about 28–37.5% of traces, the A41→A26 pair shifts from one to two steps apart, and participation rises from not observed to about 30–38% per activity with the three co-occurring in only about 0.5–1.5% of traces. Screening qualified 21 control-flow items against about 0.52 expected without change, so the ensemble is far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [DIR004, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL001, REL002, REL005, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]

Limitations: all items come from the single control-flow family and several describe the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations; the 200-trace windows cannot exclude that the three activities occurred at very low rates earlier and only became frequent (A20 shows in one earlier trace), and the small pairwise overlaps leave open whether the choice is strictly one-of-three. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that this block is a previously extremely rare path that became frequent rather than a newly added one. [OCC002]

Other differences: A02's successors moved away from A26 (about 26% of its observed outgoing transitions earlier, none later), with A16 and many small new successors taking that share; this change at A02 is not explained by the main hypothesis. [DIR001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 104 units tested, 21 items qualified, 0.52 expected without change. That's 21 items vs 0.52 expected — many times larger (about 40x). So the count cannot be explained by chance as a whole. This means we go beyond "insufficient evidence" based on the count comparison.

All evidence items are control-flow family (CF_REL, CF_LAG, CF_POS, CF_OCC, CF_DIR). No time items (TWAIT) and no resource items (ASSIGN, CONC, HAND). So I should not discuss time or resources.

Now let me understand the behavioural story.

Key activities: A19, A20, A25, A26, A41, A02.

Before window:
- A19: not observed (OCC001: participation 0 before, 0.38 after; support 0 → 76).
- A20: nearly not observed (OCC002: participation 0.005 before, 0.295 after; support 1 → 59).
- A25: not observed (OCC003: participation 0 before, 0.345 after; support 0 → 69).
- A26: observed in all traces both windows (POS004: support 1.0 both windows).
- A41: observed in all traces both windows (DIR004 support 202/203 outgoing transitions; REL items show A41 present in all traces: REL004 before B_only = 1.0 meaning A41 present, A19 absent in all 200 traces).
- A02: DIR001 shows A02's outgoing transitions changed; support 35 → 44 traces.

After window:
- A19 appears in 38% of traces (76/200), positioned around 0.35–0.37 of the trace (POS001 mean 0.37).
- A20 appears in ~29.5% of traces (59/200), position ~0.36.
- A25 appears in ~34.5% of traces (69/200), position ~0.37.
- A26 still in all traces, position slightly later (mean 0.370 → 0.396).

Relations (REL):
- REL003 (A19, A26): before, A26 present without A19 in 100% of traces (B_only = 1.0). After: cooccurrence 0.38, A_before_B (A19 before A26) 0.375, B_only 0.62. So A19 now occurs before A26 in ~37.5% of traces.
- REL008 (A25, A26): before B_only 1.0; after cooccurrence 0.345, A_before_B (A25 before A26) 0.325, B_only 0.655. A25 before A26 in ~32.5%.
- REL004 (A19, A41): before B_only 1.0; after cooccurrence 0.38, B_before_A (A41 before A19) 0.375. So A41 before A19 in ~37.5%.
- REL009 (A25, A41): before B_only 1.0; after cooccurrence 0.345, B_before_A (A41 before A25) 0.33. A41 before A25 in ~33%.
- REL007 (A20, A41): before B_only 0.995; after cooccurrence 0.295, B_before_A (A41 before A20) 0.28. A41 before A20 in ~28%.
- REL006 (A20, A26): before B_only 0.995; after cooccurrence 0.295, A_before_B (A20 before A26) 0.285. A20 before A26 in ~28.5%.
- REL001 (A19, A20): before neither 0.995 (both absent); after A_only (A19 only) 0.37, B_only (A20 only) 0.285, neither 0.335, cooccurrence 0.01. So A19 and A20 rarely occur together — they are alternatives.
- REL005 (A20, A25): before neither 0.995; after A_only (A20 only) 0.29, B_only (A25 only) 0.34, neither 0.365, cooccurrence 0.005. Again alternatives.
- REL002 (A19, A25): before neither 1.0; after A_only 0.365, B_only 0.33, neither 0.29, cooccurrence 0.015. Alternatives.

So A19, A20, A25 are mutually nearly exclusive alternatives: each appears in ~29–38% of traces, and they rarely co-occur (cooccurrence ~0.5–1.5%). Combined participation: A19 38%, A20 29.5%, A25 34.5% — sums to ~102%, consistent with exactly one of the three being chosen in most traces (with small overlap ~1-1.5% each pair, and ~29-36.5% neither... wait, let me check: neither for REL002 (A19,A25) is 0.29, meaning 29% of traces have neither A19 nor A25. A20 is in 29.5%. So traces with neither A19 nor A25 mostly have A20. Consistent with a choice among {A19, A20, A25}.

Ordering: A41 before each of A19/A20/A25 (B_before_A ~0.28–0.375), and each of A19/A20/A25 before A26 (A_before_B ~0.285–0.375). So the new pattern is: A41 → (A19 | A20 | A25) → A26.

DIR evidence:
- DIR004 (A41's outgoing): before, A41 → A26 in ~82% of A41's outgoing transitions (0.8168); after, A41 → A26 drops to ~1.5% (0.0148), and new transitions to A19 (~33%), A25 (~30%), A20 (~23.6%) appear. So A41 now leads to one of A19/A20/A25 instead of directly to A26.
- DIR003 (A25's outgoing): before empty (A25 not observed); after, A25 → A26 in 90% of outgoing transitions, plus small shares to others. So A25 leads to A26.
- DIR002 (A19's outgoing): before empty; after, A19 → A26 in ~95% of outgoing transitions. A19 leads to A26.
- DIR001 (A02's outgoing): before, A02 → A26 in ~26% of outgoing; after, A26 drops out (−0.257), A16 rises (+0.125), A45 rises, and many small new edges. Support 35 → 44 traces. This is a secondary change: A02 no longer leads to A26 as often; its outgoing profile is more spread out. Hmm, this could be a consequence: previously A02 → A26 directly; now maybe A02 → ... → A41 → choice → A26? Actually we don't know where A02 fits. The redistribution at A02 is a separate observation.

LAG001 (A41, A26): before, the pair A41 then A26 within five steps: lag 1 in 82.5%, lag 2 in 17.5%. After: lag 1 in ~1.2%, lag 2 in ~83.4%, lag 3 in ~14.1%. So A26 now follows A41 with a lag of 2 steps instead of 1 — consistent with an intermediate activity (one of A19/A20/A25) inserted between A41 and A26.

POS004 (A26): position shifts slightly later (mean 0.370 → 0.396), consistent with an inserted activity before A26.

So the main hypothesis: In the later window, a new step was inserted between A41 and A26: after A41, one of three alternative activities (A19, A20, A25) executes (mutually exclusive choice), each leading to A26. Previously A41 was followed directly by A26. This is an insertion of a new alternative block (activities added), not a shift in path frequencies between existing paths — A19, A20, A25 were (nearly) absent before.

Wait — the guidance says: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows... It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window". Here A19/A20/A25 were absent before, so this is an addition of activities, not a path-frequency shift. The hypothesis is about insertion/addition of activities.

Support level: The screening count is 21 items vs 0.52 expected — many times larger, so chance cannot explain the count. Then judge by directness, consistency, ability to rule out competitors.

The hypothesis "an activity (one of A19/A20/A25) is inserted between A41 and A26" is directly supported by:
- OCC: A19, A20, A25 go from absent to ~29–38% participation.
- DIR004: A41 → A26 (82% of outgoing) becomes A41 → A19/A25/A20 (~87% combined).
- DIR002/DIR003: A19 → A26 (95%), A25 → A26 (90%).
- REL003/REL008: A19/A25 before A26 (~33–37.5%).
- REL004/REL009/REL007: A41 before A19/A25/A20 (~28–37.5%).
- LAG001: A41→A26 lag shifts from 1 to 2.
- POS004: A26 position shifts slightly later.
- REL001/REL002/REL005: A19, A20, A25 are mutually exclusive alternatives.

This is direct, consistent relational evidence. The competing explanation: could this be a rare variant appearing? No — 76/200, 69/200, 59/200 traces, and the screening count is 40x the chance expectation. Could it be that these activities existed but weren't sampled? With 200 traces and zero occurrences, if the true participation were, say, 5%, we'd expect ~10 occurrences; zero in 200 makes that unlikely, but we can't fully rule out very rare presence. Also, the evidence can't tell us why — but we shouldn't speculate about causes anyway.

One caveat: A20's before support is 1 trace (0.5%), so A20 was nearly absent, not strictly absent. A19 and A25 had 0 support.

What about DIR001 (A02)? A02's outgoing transitions changed: A26 share dropped from ~26% to 0, A16 rose from ~8.6% to ~18%, A45 from ~14% to ~16%, and many new small edges appeared. Support 35 → 44 traces. This is a secondary difference not fully explained by the main hypothesis. Actually, could it be related? If A02 previously led to A26 directly and now the path goes through A41... but we don't have evidence about A02 → A41. The DIR001 profile shows A02 now leads to many different activities with small shares — more dispersed. Hmm, after: A16 0.18, A45 0.16, A47 0.09, A19 0.045, A32 0.045, A27 0.045... It's quite dispersed. This might reflect a different change at A02, or a consequence of rerouting. I'll report it under "Other differences".

Also POS004 (A26 position slightly later) is part of the main hypothesis (consistent with insertion before A26). LAG001 likewise.

Now, the support level: Supported hypothesis. The evidence directly shows: A41 previously flowed directly to A26 (82% of A41's outgoing transitions, lag 1 in 82.5% of A41→A26 pairs); in the later window A41 flows to one of A19/A20/A25 (~87% combined), each of which flows to A26 (90–95% of their outgoing), and the A41→A26 lag shifts to 2 steps. The three new activities are mutually exclusive alternatives. Participation ~29–38% each.

The main hypothesis: a block of three alternative activities (A19, A20, A25) was inserted between A41 and A26 — i.e., in the later window, traces typically run A41 → (A19 or A20 or A25) → A26, whereas before they ran A41 → A26 directly.

Limitations: A20 was observed in only 1 before-trace, so strictly it went from nearly absent to present; the evidence cannot show whether these activities existed at very low rates before; POS/LAG use event positions, not clock time — but here we have DIR and REL evidence showing the actual successor change, so placement is directly supported. Also, all items come from one family (control flow) and several describe the same underlying trace behaviour, so they are not independent confirmations.

Competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out: that the three activities are a rerouting of flow that previously went elsewhere (e.g., A02's changed outgoing profile suggests other routing also changed), or that the "insertion" is actually a shift of an existing rare path into a frequent one — with 200-trace windows we cannot exclude that A19/A20/A25 occurred at very low rates before. Also DIR001's change at A02 is not explained by the main hypothesis.

Hmm, should the level be "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? Criteria: "Supported hypothesis: the evidence supports a specific hypothesis directly and consistently." The insertion between A41 and A26 is shown directly by DIR004 (A41's successors changed from A26 to A19/A20/A25), DIR002/DIR003 (A19/A25 lead to A26), REL items (A41 before each; each before A26), LAG001 (lag 1 → 2), OCC (participation from 0 to 29–38%). This is direct and consistent. The screening count (21 vs 0.52) rules out chance as a whole. I'd say Supported hypothesis.

The competing explanation: the evidence cannot rule out that the three activities existed at very low frequency before (A20 had 1 trace) and simply became frequent — but that's still a change. Actually a better competing framing: whether the inserted block is a genuinely new path or a previously extremely rare path that became frequent; also the DIR001 change at A02 suggests additional routing changes not covered by the main hypothesis. Also, several items describe the same traces, so they aren't independent.

- A25: 0 → 34.5% (69/200).
- A41 → A26: ~82% of A41's observed outgoing transitions before → ~1.5% after; A41 → A19/A25/A20 ≈ 33%/30%/24% after.

Bullets:

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Main hypothesis: In the later window, a choice among three mutually exclusive activities (A19, A20, A25) is inserted between A41 and A26: traces that previously ran A41 → A26 now run A41 → (A19 or A20 or A25) → A26. Supporting signs: A41's outgoing transitions moved from A26 (~82%) to the three new activities (~87% combined); each new activity leads to A26; the A41→A26 lag shifted from 1 to 2 steps; participation of the three went from absent to ~29–38%; 21 qualifying items against 0.52 expected by chance. Limitations: all items belong to the control-flow family and several describe the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations; with 200-trace windows the evidence cannot exclude that the three activities occurred at very low rates before (A20 appeared in one earlier trace) rather than being entirely new; POS/LAG use event positions, though the successor change at A41 shows the placement directly.

Other differences: A02's outgoing routing changed (A26 no longer a successor; A16 and others gained), which the insertion hypothesis does not explain. [DIR001]

Competing explanation: the change at A02 could indicate a broader rerouting that the evidence does not fully connect; also cannot rule out that the alternative block was an extremely rare pre-existing path rather than a new one.

Also: "If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:' without adding their activities to the main hypothesis."

I think "Supported hypothesis" is right.
